case-sara.text: [Quietly] When I said I miss being someone's first call, I felt something in my chest. Anyway, I should probably change my phone plan.
case-sara.suggestion: The phone plan may need sorting too. Would you like to pause with what you felt when you said ‘someone's first call’ before we move on?

case-sara.text: [Laughs, eyes wet] Coming home hurts. Listen to me — a whole tragedy over a takeaway dinner.
case-sara.suggestion: You laughed just as you said coming home hurts. Could we stay with that hurt for a moment, if you want to?

case-sara.text: [Quickly] I wanted him to ask how my day was. But he worked long hours, and his team was understaffed, so obviously—
case-sara.suggestion: You were just touching how much you wanted him to ask. Would it be useful to stay with that wanting before we work out his reasons?

case-sara.text: [Pauses, then brightens] I felt really alone on Sunday. Oh, I forgot to tell you about the campaign at work.
case-sara.suggestion: There was a pause when you said ‘alone’. Does that still need some room, or is the work story what you want to bring in now?

case-sara.text: [Looks down] I was hurt that he forgot. But it was just a date. Other people have real problems.
case-sara.suggestion: It was just a date, and being forgotten hurt. Would you be willing to give that hurt a little room without comparing it with anyone else's?

case-sara.text: [Sighs] I wish I could tell him I was lonely. Maybe I should start with a list of what I did wrong.
case-sara.suggestion: Before the list, you said you wished you could tell him you were lonely. Is that something you want us to stay with?

case-sara.text: [Voice softens, then speeds up] I wanted to be held. Actually, what's the research on attachment styles?
case-sara.suggestion: I can answer that. I also heard your voice soften at ‘held’. Would you prefer the explanation now, or a moment with what being held means to you?

case-sara.text: [Tears, then checks watch] I hate eating alone. Sorry, did I tell you what time my train leaves?
case-sara.suggestion: We should make sure you catch it. Once we've checked the time, would you like a little space for how eating alone feels?

case-sara.text: [Shrugs] I started to feel sad, then I thought: this is just what happens when dopamine drops after a relationship.
case-sara.suggestion: That explanation may help you make sense of it. Would it also help to notice the sadness that came just before it, or would you rather leave it there today?

case-sara.text: [Quiet, then joking] I wanted to matter to him. Well, at least my delivery app misses me.
case-sara.suggestion: You went to a joke just after saying you wanted to matter. If it feels okay, could we return to those words, ‘I wanted to matter’?

case-sara.text: [Looks away] I was angry he never asked what I needed. But let me explain the whole timeline first.
case-sara.suggestion: The timeline might help. Before we go through it, do you want to stay with that anger about not being asked what you needed?

case-sara.text: [After a pause] That empty feeling is back. I don't want to go into it today; I need to talk about getting through tonight.
case-sara.suggestion: Let's focus on tonight. We can leave the empty feeling there for now. What feels hardest about getting through the evening?

case-arne.text: [Soft, then brisk] I miss her at breakfast. Anyway, the kettle needs descaling.
case-arne.suggestion: The kettle may need attention too. Would you like a moment with missing her before we move on?

case-arne.text: [Eyes wet, small laugh] That coat still smells like her. Silly old coat.
case-arne.suggestion: You laughed as it brought her close. Would you like to stay with what you noticed?

case-arne.text: [Softly, then listing] I wanted company. Tom’s busy, Emma works, the neighbors—
case-arne.suggestion: Before we list everyone’s schedules, would you like to hear that wish for company a little more?

case-arne.text: [Voice catches] I needed rest too. But the hospital parking was expensive.
case-arne.suggestion: We can discuss the parking. Would it help first to pause with needing rest?

case-arne.text: [Quickly] I was angry. Of course, everyone meant well, so forget that.
case-arne.suggestion: Their intentions matter, and your anger showed up too. Would you like to give it a little room?

case-arne.text: [Soft, then technical] Seeing her recipe hurt. The ink’s probably fading chemically.
case-arne.suggestion: That may explain the ink. Would you like to stay with what hurt when you saw the recipe?

case-arne.text: [Pauses, then brisk] I’m lonely. Right, shall I tell you about the roof instead?
case-arne.suggestion: We can choose either. Would you like a moment with “lonely,” or is the roof what you need today?

case-arne.text: [Tearful, changes topic] Her laugh. I miss it. Did it rain here yesterday?
case-arne.suggestion: We can talk about yesterday. I also heard how much you miss her laugh. Would you like to return to that?

case-arne.text: [Soft, then self-critical] I wanted Emma to stay. That’s enough of my complaints.
case-arne.suggestion: Wanting her to stay doesn’t have to be a complaint. Would you like to hear that wish before leaving it?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] You noticed I changed the subject. I’d rather keep it changed today.
case-arne.suggestion: Then we will. What would you like us to focus on instead?

case-arne.text: [Quiet, then hurried] I enjoyed the workshop. Never mind, I forgot to pay a bill.
case-arne.suggestion: Is the bill urgent now, or would you like a moment with enjoying the workshop first?

case-arne.text: [Smiles through tears] I’d like to remember her teasing. But I’m getting sentimental.
case-arne.suggestion: That memory seems to bring warmth and tears. Would you like to stay with it, without judging it?

case-arne.text: [Voice softens, then lists] I wanted rest. The appointments were Monday, Wednesday, sometimes Friday—
case-arne.suggestion: The schedule shows the demands. Would you like to pause with wanting rest before we list more?

case-arne.text: [Eyes wet, jokes] Nobody to tell my day to. At least the kettle listens.
case-arne.suggestion: The joke came beside that loneliness. Would you like to stay with either, or leave it there?

case-arne.text: [Quiet, then analytical] I liked the quiet. Probably just my nervous system adjusting.
case-arne.suggestion: That may be part of it. Would it help to hear what liking the quiet means to you too?

case-arne.text: [Voice catches, then brisk] I wanted Emma to notice. But she’s busy, let’s discuss her job.
case-arne.suggestion: Her job matters. Before we move there, do you want a moment with wanting her to notice?

case-arne.text: [Frowning, then laughing] I’m angry when they speak for Eva. Well, everyone’s an expert.
case-arne.suggestion: There’s humor and anger here. Would you like to hear what your anger is saying?

case-arne.text: [Softly, then hurried] I miss her teasing. Right, should I tell you about the plumbing?
case-arne.suggestion: Is the plumbing what you need now, or would staying with that warm memory be welcome?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] I changed the subject because I needed a break. Not because I’m scared.
case-arne.suggestion: Thank you for making that clear. We’ll take the break rather than pull you back.

case-arne.text: [Quiet, then blaming himself] I wanted help. Listen to me, making everything about myself.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we pause before that judgment and hear the need for help, if you want?

case-arne.text: [Tearful, then explanatory] I’m lonely. Of course, statistically, plenty of people live alone.
case-arne.suggestion: That’s true. Would you like to stay with how living alone feels for you, rather than the numbers?

case-arne.text: [Softly, then practical] Rest felt good. But I do need the benefits form sorted today.
case-arne.suggestion: Then let’s make time for the form. Do you want to leave the feeling there or briefly name it first?

case-arne.text: [Voice lowers, then speeds up] I don’t want to lose her laugh. Anyway, here’s the history of that photograph—
case-arne.suggestion: Would you like to pause with not wanting to lose her laugh before the photograph’s history?

case-arne.text: [Quiet, small smile] I enjoyed myself. Don’t make a big thing of it.
case-arne.suggestion: We needn’t make it big. Would you like a small moment with the enjoyment, or shall we go on?

case-arne.text: [Tender, then brisk] Her laugh gets to me. But I don’t want to stay there today.
case-arne.suggestion: We won’t pull you back. Where would you like the conversation to go?

case-arne.text: [Voice softens, then technical] I wanted someone to notice. The care rota was poorly designed.
case-arne.suggestion: The rota may matter. Would you like to return briefly to wanting someone to notice, or stay with the practical failure?

case-arne.text: [Eyes wet, jokes] That’s me being sentimental. Now, the weather—
case-arne.suggestion: Would you welcome a moment with what moved you, or is the change of subject a pause you need?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] Yes, I changed the subject. I’m choosing it, not hiding.
case-arne.suggestion: I hear that choice. We’ll follow the subject you want, without treating it as hiding.

case-arne.text: [Quiet, then listing] I missed having help. But Emma’s shifts are long, Tom’s knee—
case-arne.suggestion: Those limits are real. Before considering them, would hearing what help you wanted be useful?

case-arne.text: [Warm, then brisk] The workshop felt good. Don’t pin me there; I also need to talk about money.
case-arne.suggestion: We can turn to money. Would you like to leave one word for the good moment first, or move straight on?

case-arne.text: [Voice catches, then self-critical] I wanted rest. I’ve said that too many times now.
case-arne.suggestion: Does repeating it feel unhelpful, or does that judgment arrive when the need comes close? We can choose where to go.

case-arne.text: [Quiet, then explaining] I wanted Emma to stay. In our family we’ve always made a lot of showing up—
case-arne.suggestion: Would you like a moment with your own wish before the broader explanation, or does the history help you today?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] That pause wasn’t avoidance. I was finding the words.
case-arne.suggestion: Thank you for correcting me. Take the time you need; I won’t redirect the pause.

case-arne.text: [Soft, then analytical] I’m angry. Is that one of those grief stages?
case-arne.suggestion: There’s no stage we need to assign you. Would you like to hear this particular anger, or discuss your question first?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] If we return to that feeling, I want one minute, not the whole session.
case-arne.suggestion: One minute, with your choice to stop sooner. Then we’ll check where you want to go.

case-arne.text: [Voice softens, then brisk] I miss her. I also genuinely want this form sorted. Both.
case-arne.suggestion: Both matter. Would you prefer the form first, with an option to return to the missing later?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then brisk] I miss the drawing. Anyway, I should buy a better pencil case.
case-mia.suggestion: Before the pencil case, would you like to stay with what you miss, or leave it for today?

case-mia.text: [Angry, then factual] I wasn’t asked. The bag has two handles, actually.
case-mia.suggestion: I noticed we moved to the handles. Could we return to not being asked, if that feels useful?

case-mia.text: [Tearful, then laughs] It hurt. Oh well, everyone has bad days.
case-mia.suggestion: Would it be okay to hear what hurt before putting it with everyone’s bad days?

case-mia.text: [Quietly, changes topic] I needed him to listen. Have you seen the weather forecast?
case-mia.suggestion: Could we pause at wanting him to listen? You can also tell me if you need a break.

case-mia.text: [Sad, then lists] I felt alone. Tuesday was the meeting, Wednesday was the tour...
case-mia.suggestion: Could we return to that feeling of being alone, rather than the schedule, for a moment?

case-mia.text: [Moved, then dismisses] Being asked was lovely. A small thing, really.
case-mia.suggestion: That lovely part seemed to matter. Would you like to give it a little more room?

case-mia.text: [Guilty, then general] I hated how I spoke. Couples argue, don’t they?
case-mia.suggestion: We can talk generally, or return to what bothered you about your own words. Which would help?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then practical] I miss giving the tour. I could review the rota instead.
case-mia.suggestion: Is reviewing the rota what you need now, or would you like to stay with missing the tour?

case-mia.text: [Fearful, then smiles] Tomorrow scares me. Never mind, it’ll probably be fine.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we hear a little of what scares you, without having to decide how tomorrow will go?

case-mia.text: [Firm] I want to stop talking about the sadness and plan how to ask for the chair.
case-mia.suggestion: Let’s turn to asking for the chair. We don’t need to bring you back to the sadness.

case-mia.text: [Tired] I changed the subject because I need a rest.
case-mia.suggestion: Thank you for saying so. Let’s rest rather than return to that subject now.

case-mia.text: [Warm, then shrugs] I liked being useful. But it’s not a big deal.
case-mia.suggestion: Would you like to linger with liking that, before deciding how big a deal it is?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then brisk] I miss the old evenings. I should find more suitable pencils.
case-mia.suggestion: Would it help to stay with missing the evenings before we turn to equipment?

case-mia.text: [Angry, then excuses] I wanted a say. But Alex had a busy day, so never mind.
case-mia.suggestion: His day can matter too. Would you like us to return to what having a say meant there?

case-mia.text: [Moved, then factual] Sam waited for me. The meeting agenda had six things on it.
case-mia.suggestion: I noticed we moved to the agenda. Could we pause with what his waiting meant to you?

case-mia.text: [Uneasy, then smiles] I felt watched. I’m probably lucky anyone cares.
case-mia.suggestion: Before deciding you should feel lucky, would you like to hear the uncomfortable part?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then lists] I miss contributing. There are still emails I could answer.
case-mia.suggestion: Are the emails the direction you want now, or could we stay briefly with what you miss?

case-mia.text: [Guilty, then general] I regret snapping. Communication is complicated for everyone.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we return to your own regret, rather than communication generally, if you want to explore it?

case-mia.text: [Relieved, then dismisses] I liked choosing. Such a trivial thing to talk about.
case-mia.suggestion: The relief seemed important before “trivial” arrived. Would you like to stay with it a moment?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’ve moved to the practical part because I need something concrete now.
case-mia.suggestion: Let’s follow that. What concrete part would be most useful with the time and energy left?

case-mia.text: [Fearful, then brisk] I’m scared of losing more. I should read the museum newsletter.
case-mia.suggestion: Would you like to return to that fear, or is the newsletter a needed change of pace?

case-mia.text: [Warm, then changes topic] Being sisters again felt good. Did I mention Ella’s kitchen?
case-mia.suggestion: Could we linger with “being sisters again” before we move to the kitchen?

case-mia.text: [Tired, firm] I know the feeling is there. Going back to it won’t help today.
case-mia.suggestion: We can leave it there. Let’s choose something that fits what you need today.

case-mia.text: [Sad, then jokes] I felt outside the conversation. At least the tea was good.
case-mia.suggestion: The tea can have been good. Would it be okay to return to feeling outside the conversation?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then precise] I miss the drawing. The paper is actually the wrong weight.
case-mia.suggestion: Is the paper the part you want to work on, or could we return briefly to the missing?

case-mia.text: [Angry, then qualifies] I wanted him to wait. He usually does. It’s unfair to dwell on this.
case-mia.suggestion: His usual care can stay in view. Would you like to return to what happened in this one moment?

case-mia.text: [Moved, then brisk] I felt included. We should discuss next week’s schedule.
case-mia.suggestion: Is the schedule urgent now, or can we give feeling included a little room first?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I changed the subject because your question didn’t fit, not because it got close.
case-mia.suggestion: Thanks for correcting that. Which part would you like us to return to with a better question?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then abstract] I’m sad. Adjustment to illness is a complex process, obviously.
case-mia.suggestion: Would it be useful to return from the general process to what is sad for you here?

case-mia.text: [Warm, then dismisses] That conversation felt like home. Just a turn of phrase.
case-mia.suggestion: We needn’t make it bigger. Would you like to hear what “home” caught in that conversation?

case-mia.text: [Firm] I know you want to return to the hurt. I need to sort out the actual request first.
case-mia.suggestion: Let’s follow the request. We can leave the hurt without treating that choice as a problem.

case-mia.text: [Guilty, then lists] I regret the tone. The bag, the plants, the laundry... there’s a lot.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we stay with one moment of regret rather than add more tasks, if you have room for that?

case-mia.text: [Tired, corrects] I didn’t move away from the feeling. I ran out of words.
case-mia.suggestion: We can let the words run out. Would quiet company fit better than returning with another question?

case-mia.text: [Fearful, then practical] I don’t know what I’ll manage. I should find a better calendar app.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we hear the uncertainty before the app, or is planning the more useful direction today?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then jokes] There goes the afternoon. At least I’m not buying expensive pencils.
case-mia.suggestion: The joke changes the pace. Would you like to return to losing the afternoon, or leave it here?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m not going back to that today. I’ve said enough to know what I need.
case-mia.suggestion: We can respect that. Let’s stay with what you now know you need.

case-nora.text: [Hurt, then brisk] I couldn’t look at the drawings. The printer needed fixing anyway.
case-nora.suggestion: Would you like to return to not wanting to look, before we move to the printer?

case-nora.text: [Angry, then laughs] My answer wasn’t enough. Classic office chat, I suppose.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we hear what that did to you before making it ordinary office chat?

case-nora.text: [Sad, then factual] I wanted my work seen. The project has three floors.
case-nora.suggestion: I noticed we moved to the floors. Would it help to return to wanting your work seen?

case-nora.text: [Moved, then dismisses] Lina listened. It was nothing special.
case-nora.suggestion: That seemed to matter a moment ago. Would you like to stay with what was good?

case-nora.text: [Fearful, then practical] I’m scared to raise it. I should organize the files first.
case-nora.suggestion: Are the files what you need now, or could we pause with the fear?

case-nora.text: [Quietly, changes topic] I felt alone. Did I tell you about the new camera?
case-nora.suggestion: Could we linger with feeling alone, or would you prefer a change of subject?

case-nora.text: [Angry, then excuses] Max spoke over me. He was trying to help, though.
case-nora.suggestion: His intention can matter too. Would you like to return to what it was like for you?

case-nora.text: [Sad, then general] It hurt. People say thoughtless things.
case-nora.suggestion: Would it be useful to return from people generally to what hurt in this moment?

case-nora.text: [Relieved, then shrugs] I liked being asked. Not worth talking about, really.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we give that relief a little room before dismissing it?

case-nora.text: [Firm] I want to stop exploring and work on what I’ll ask Max.
case-nora.suggestion: Let’s turn to that request. We don’t need to bring you back to the feeling.

case-nora.text: [Tired] I changed the subject because I need a break.
case-nora.suggestion: We can take the break. Returning to the topic can wait.

case-nora.text: [Warm, then brisk] I enjoyed the photographs. Anyway, back to the awful meeting.
case-nora.suggestion: Would you like the enjoyable moment to have some space before we return to the meeting?

case-nora.text: [Hurt, then qualifies] I wanted my work seen. The firm does good work, to be fair.
case-nora.suggestion: That can stay true. Would you like to return to what you wanted seen in this moment?

case-nora.text: [Angry, then excuses] I wanted Max to wait. He must have felt awkward too.
case-nora.suggestion: His awkwardness can matter. Could we also return to what waiting would have given you?

case-nora.text: [Sad, then lists] It hurt. First the meeting, then the email, then the lunch...
case-nora.suggestion: Would it help to stay with one hurtful moment instead of gathering the whole sequence?

case-nora.text: [Moved, then jokes] Lina listened. Maybe she just likes a dramatic story.
case-nora.suggestion: Before the joke, could we hear what her listening meant to you?

case-nora.text: [Uneasy, then abstract] I was unsettled. Social dynamics are complicated.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we return from the general dynamics to what was unsettled for you?

case-nora.text: [Warm, then dismisses] I enjoyed dinner. That’s hardly therapy material.
case-nora.suggestion: Would you like to give that enjoyment a place here before moving on?

case-nora.text: [Firm] I need to look at practical support before I go back to the feeling.
case-nora.suggestion: Let’s follow that priority. What support would you like to consider?

case-nora.text: [Fearful, then brisk] I’m afraid I’ll be reduced to a complaint. I should sort the presentation slides.
case-nora.suggestion: Are the slides what you need now, or could we pause with that fear?

case-nora.text: [Guilty, then general] I regret snapping at Adam. Relationships are hard.
case-nora.suggestion: Would you like to return to your own regret rather than relationships generally?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I moved away because I didn’t want that question, not because I didn’t want the topic.
case-nora.suggestion: Thanks for clarifying. What part of the topic would you like us to return to?

case-nora.text: [Tired, firm] I know there’s hurt. I don’t have room for more of it today.
case-nora.suggestion: We can leave it there. Let’s choose a direction that fits today.

case-nora.text: [Relieved, then brisk] I liked having the choice. Back to what I should have said...
case-nora.suggestion: Could we stay briefly with liking the choice before judging the response?

case-nora.text: [Hurt, then precise] I couldn’t look at the drawings. The dimensions were wrong on one sheet.
case-nora.suggestion: Is that sheet what you want to work on, or could we return to what made looking difficult?

case-nora.text: [Angry, then qualifies] I wanted Max to wait. He gets so many other things right.
case-nora.suggestion: We can keep that in view. Would you like to return to what you wanted in this moment?

case-nora.text: [Moved, then brisk] I felt heard. We should make a list of all my options.
case-nora.suggestion: Is the list needed now, or would it help to stay briefly with feeling heard?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I changed the subject because the image didn’t fit. Not because it was too close.
case-nora.suggestion: Thanks for correcting it. What part would you like us to return to without that image?

case-nora.text: [Sad, then abstract] I miss the work. Organizational inclusion is a complicated subject.
case-nora.suggestion: Would it be useful to come back from the general subject to what you personally miss?

case-nora.text: [Warm, then dismisses] I liked the dinner. That’s not the point of being here.
case-nora.suggestion: We needn’t make it the whole point. Would you like that ordinary enjoyment to have some room?

case-nora.text: [Firm] I need to choose practical support before we return to the hurt.
case-nora.suggestion: Let’s follow that. Returning to the hurt needn’t come first.

case-nora.text: [Guilty, then lists] I regret snapping. The meeting, the call, the dinner... it’s a lot.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we stay with one moment of regret, rather than add the whole day, if you have room?

case-nora.text: [Tired, corrects] I didn’t leave the feeling. I ran out of words.
case-nora.suggestion: We can let the words run out. Would quiet company fit better than another question?

case-nora.text: [Uneasy, then practical] I don’t know what today meant. I should redesign the slide template.
case-nora.suggestion: Is the template a useful direction, or would you like to stay with what remains unclear?

case-nora.text: [Sad, then jokes] My work got seen without me. At least the drawings don’t need lunch.
case-nora.suggestion: The joke shifts the pace. Would you like to return to that loss, or leave it for now?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I’ve said enough to know what I need. Going back would cost more than it gives today.
case-nora.suggestion: We can respect that. Let’s stay with what you now know you need.
